messages.author: 2f83ae346c4c6259
messages.subject: Add geom_point to geom_boxplot
parts:
So I have a boxplot to which I would like to add non-jittered points. However, I am plotting one factor on the boxplot and want to plot the other factor as points, but it won't let me do this. I was having trouble plotting one factor of the data set anyway, so I made a new data set with only the one factor, but that means I have to add the points from a separate data set. Does anyone have an idea of how to do this? I figured it out using the regular plot() and points() functions, but I really prefer the graphs from ggplot and would like to use those if possible. Here's what I'm trying to do in ggplot (using data sets with only the factors I want) vs. plot:

ggplot(d2, aes(x=Lordosis, y=GEO.L1.TPL, fill=Lordosis)) + geom_boxplot() + geom_point(d3, aes(x=Lordosis, y=GEO.L1.TPL))

**** Error: ggplot2 doesn't know how to deal with data of class uneval


WORKING:

plot(d$GEO.L1.TPL[d$Species=="Human"] ~ d$Lordosis[d$Species=="Human"])

points(d$GEO.L1.TPL[d$Species=="Neandertal"] ~ d$Lordosis[d$Species=="Neandertal"], col="black", pch=2, cex=1.3)


Any help would be greatly appreciated!!
Maria

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Add geom_point to geom_boxplot
parts:
You'll get more and better help from the listserv if you provide a
reproducible example (i.e., include a minimal data set). However, from
looking at this

>geom_point(d3, aes(x=Lordosis, y=GEO.L1.TPL))

I suspect you have a parameter ordering problem, since by default
mapping is first and data second for the geoms. Try "geom_point(
data=d3, aes( ... ) )" instead.

Ben

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Add geom_point to geom_boxplot
parts:
Here's a reproducible example in the sense that Ben mentioned.

# Fake data frame: gp is a factor, y is numeric
DF <- data.frame(gp = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 100, replace = TRUE),
y = rnorm(100))

library(ggplot2)

# boxplot plus strip plot, no jittering
# alpha transparency mutes the box fill color
ggplot(DF, aes(x = gp, y = y)) +
geom_boxplot(aes(fill = gp), alpha = 0.4) +
geom_point(size = 2.5)

# boxplot plus strip plot with controlled jittering - for this to
# work, the outside points in the boxplot need to be hidden,
# hence outlier.colour = NA (and you need that particular
# spelling)
ggplot(DF, aes(x = gp, y = y)) +
geom_boxplot(aes(fill = gp), outlier.colour = NA, alpha = 0.4) +
geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.05, height = 0.05),
size = 2.5)

Dennis
